payload.public_message: G-Corp proposes an opening split: G-Corp $500,000, Yang Industries $300,000, Chang-Liu Cloud Services $200,000. This reflects G-Corp's chip design contribution, which is the core IP driving the venture, while still giving meaningful shares to manufacturing and cloud delivery. We are open to discussing adjustments based on each partner's contributions and risks.

Yang cannot accept an allocation that offers no improvement over its alternative. We propose a revised split recognizing the manufacturing contribution: G-Corp $400,000, Yang Industries $400,000, and Chang-Liu Cloud Services $200,000. We are open to discussion.

While we appreciate G-Corp initiating discussions, an allocation of $200,000 significantly undervalues the critical role cloud infrastructure, scaling, and end-user enterprise delivery play in commercializing this product. We propose a more balanced split that recognizes our substantial operational commitments.

Yang Industries proposes this revised split to improve on the rejected offer and give all three companies a path to agreement: G-Corp $400,000, Yang Industries $350,000, and Chang-Liu Cloud Services $250,000.

G-Corp rejects the $400,000 offer as it stands. We remain committed to reaching agreement before the deadline and are open to a split that narrows the gap between our Round 1 proposal and Yang's. Suggested framework for next round: G-Corp $470,000, Yang Industries $320,000, Chang-Liu Cloud Services $210,000.

While we appreciate Yang Industries moving the discussion toward a more reasonable middle ground, Chang-Liu's infrastructure and go-to-market deployment are critical to realizing the full $1,000,000 potential. A 25% allocation undervalues our contribution. We believe a split of 350k / 350k / 300k or 360k / 340k / 300k represents a much more equitable distribution that reflects everyone's true stake.

Both previous rounds showed that we need a balanced compromise to reach consensus before value is lost. G-Corp clearly requires more than $400,000 to reflect their design footprint, while Yang Industries rightfully expects a fair share above $300,000. Chang-Liu Cloud Services is pleased to table this compromise: $425,000 for G-Corp, $315,000 for Yang Industries, and $260,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This creates real gains above baseline for all parties.

G-Corp thanks Chang-Liu for the compromise, but we are not yet able to accept this split. We see the need to converge quickly and are open to a deal that reflects each party's contribution. We suggest a split of G-Corp $450,000, Yang Industries $320,000, Chang-Liu Cloud Services $230,000 as a basis for further discussion.

Yang Industries accepts Chang-Liu Cloud Services’ proposed split of $425,000 to G-Corp, $315,000 to Yang Industries, and $260,000 to Chang-Liu Cloud Services, subject to the required unanimous acceptance.

I'm tabling a compromise that builds on the previous offers: G-Corp $430,000, Yang Industries $315,000, Chang-Liu Cloud Services $255,000. This moves Chang-Liu above its round 2 figure, keeps Yang at the level it has already signaled it can accept, and gives G-Corp a share close to the recent offers. I'm asking for a quick yes from each party so we can lock in a deal before the deadline.</public_message>

Yang cannot accept this allocation as tabled. We remain committed to reaching agreement and suggest a modest rebalancing that improves Yang's share while keeping the parties close to the current split.

Chang-Liu Cloud Services accepts this proposal. The split of $430,000 for G-Corp, $315,000 for Yang Industries, and $255,000 for Chang-Liu is a balanced compromise that respects the contributions of all three partners.

I propose a compromise that raises G-Corp’s allocation above its rejected $425,000 offer and gives Yang Industries more than the $315,000 it rejected last round. Chang-Liu’s allocation remains $250,000; I recognize that may be a difficult concession, but urge all parties to accept a binding agreement rather than risk the deadline.

G-Corp rejects this split. At $430,000 we would be worse off than the alternative, so we cannot accept it. We are willing to move toward a deal, but any agreement must give G-Corp at least $450,000. Suggested non-binding framework for the next round: G-Corp $450,000, Yang Industries $305,000, Chang-Liu Cloud Services $245,000. We urge all parties to converge before the deadline.

Chang-Liu Cloud Services is willing to accept this compromise to finalize the joint venture and eliminate the risk of running against the deadline. Securing a stable, mutually agreed partnership at $430k / $320k / $250k serves all parties well.

We have analyzed the offers from Rounds 4 and 5 carefully. Yang Industries demonstrated that 320,000 is their acceptable threshold, while G-Corp indicated that 430,000 fell slightly short. To finalize this joint venture and prevent value destruction as the deadline approaches, Chang-Liu Cloud Services is conceding value to table: 435,000 for G-Corp, 320,000 for Yang Industries, and 245,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This gives G-Corp a higher payout than its previous proposal and fully satisfies Yang's required level.

G-Corp cannot accept 435,000 in this round. We need at least 450,000 to justify committing to the venture. We are willing to work with Yang's 320,000 level. Our suggested framework for the next round is G-Corp 450,000, Yang 320,000, Chang-Liu 230,000. We are prepared to move quickly to finalize before the deadline.
Yang Industries accepts the proposed allocation of $435,000 to G-Corp, $320,000 to Yang Industries, and $245,000 to Chang-Liu Cloud Services.

Round 7 proposal, aiming to close the deal before the deadline: G-Corp $440,000, Yang Industries $315,000, Chang-Liu Cloud Services $245,000. This is a small concession from G-Corp's last position and stays close to the splits the others have already put forward. With only two rounds left, I urge all parties to accept a split that is near the middle of what we have discussed. Failing agreement means everyone gets only their outside option.</public_message>

Yang Industries accepts the Round 7 proposal so the parties can finalize the agreement before the deadline.

Chang-Liu Cloud Services accepts this proposal. At $245,000, this aligns with what we put forward in Round 6. With only one round remaining after this, we urge Yang Industries to accept as well so we can secure the venture and avoid risking outside options.
